summary: GiveWell's spreadsheet "2022 GiveWell cost-effectiveness analysis — Nutrition International [March 2022]", linked from 2 of its grant pages. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values. The Chad column, the grant's location, is used: more than ten times its peers because GiveWell's 2022 figures for Chad combine a high baseline child death rate (17.8 per 1,000 child-years, against 6.5 in Angola) with a low cost per child ($3.30 a year), before its later models for Chad revised both.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs that mostly buy and hand out goods (nets, drugs, supplements, vaccines, water treatment): staff pay is a small part of the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Delivery staff are mostly hired locally at local rates, so the gap is small. Our judgment.

Share of the full cost paid in cash
